question: Türkiye is continuing with flagrantly dangerous military actions in the airspace of EU Member States, with the safety of civil aviation now also at risk.

On 19 August, Turkish military aircraft TUAF770, which was flying in the Nicosia FIR, failed to respond to calls from the Nicosia Area Control Centre, having deviated from its designated course, and proceeded to move towards the same flight level as passenger Boeing 737-800.

A few days later, a Turkish UAV violated Greek airspace, its presence in the Alexandroupoli area affecting the flight path of a commercial flight and triggering the deployment of F-16 fighter jets. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How does it intend to respond to repeated Turkish actions that undermine the safety of civil aviation?
Will the systematic disregard for air traffic rules by a candidate country and actions that threaten the safety of commercial flights and passengers in the EU continue to be accepted?
When will Türkiye face concrete consequences and sanctions for this dangerous behaviour?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.10.2026) In the Türkiye 2025 report, the Commission has underlined that the lack of adequate communication between air traffic control centres in Türkiye and Cyprus continued to compromise air safety in the Nicosia flight information region, requiring an operational solution1.

Additionally, the Commission has stressed that the flights of Turkish unmanned aerial vehicles in the flight information region and national airspace of the Republic of Cyprus also continued unabated.

The EU has a strategic interest in a secure and stable environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and remains committed to defending its interests and those of its Member States as well as to upholding regional stability. A comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus issue would significantly contribute to sustainable stability and security in the Eastern Mediterranean.

In this context, the EU remains fully committed to the reunification of Cyprus with the aim of achieving a functional and viable comprehensive settlement in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and in line with the principles, values and legislation of the EU.
